chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the verse of zakat was revealed —
'Take charity out of their wealth to cleanse them and purify them thereby' [9:103]

and it was revealed in the month of Ramadan. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered his herald, who called out among the people: 'God has imposed zakat upon you just as He has imposed salat upon you.'

So God, Mighty and Majestic, imposed it upon them from gold and silver, and He imposed the charity from camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. He called out among them with that during the month of Ramadan, and excused them from what was besides that.

He said: Then He did not impose anything on their wealth until a year had passed over them from the next year. They fasted and broke their fast. So he ordered his herald, who called out among the Muslims: 'O Muslims! Purify your wealth — your prayers will be accepted!' He said: Then he dispatched the agents of the charity and the agents of the tax.

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory annual alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Sadaqa — charity; in this context used as a synonym for zakat
key_terms.الطَّسُوق: Tassuq — tax or kharaj; a term for financial levies collected by the Islamic state
key_terms.الْحَوْل: Hawl — the full lunar year that must pass before zakat becomes due on wealth
key_terms.عُمَّال: Ummal — agents, collectors; those dispatched to collect zakat and taxes
key_terms.مُنَادِي: Munadi — the Prophet's public herald who announced religious and civic matters

ai.seo_question: When was zakat made obligatory in Islam and what are its categories?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the circumstances of the initial revelation of the zakat obligation during the month of Ramadan, when the Prophet publicly announced it through his herald. The hadith specifies the eight categories of zakatable property — gold, silver, camels, cattle, sheep, wheat, barley, dates, and raisins — and notes that all other wealth was initially exempted. The following year, after the Muslims completed another Ramadan fast, the Prophet reinforced the obligation by linking zakat payment to the acceptance of prayer, then organized formal collection agents.
